sents.t: The wedding was on a sunny Saturday in May at a beautiful old church.
The party was in a big white tent in Ana’s parents’ garden.
When Ana walked down the aisle in her white dress, Carlos was smiling and crying at the same time.
Ana’s little niece was throwing flower petals, and her nephew was carrying the rings on a small pillow.
During the ceremony, Carlos and Ana said their vows in English and in Spanish.
Then the priest said, “You may kiss the bride!” and everyone cheered.
At the reception, a mariachi band played, and we ate tacos, rice, and chicken.
Carlos’s brother, Luis, was the best man.
He gave a very funny speech.
I don’t dance well, but Ana’s grandmother pulled me onto the dance floor.
While we were dancing, she was teaching me Spanish words.
At the end of the night, Ana threw her bouquet.
Everyone looked at me, and my face turned as red as a tomato.

comp.q: Where was the party after the wedding?
o: in a tent in Ana’s parents’ garden
